config_name: XPS 16 Creator Edition — RTX Spark N1X (20-core) + RTX 6144-core GPU, 64GB, 1TB, 16" 3.2K OLED touch

specs.cpu: NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X (20-core Arm CPU, up to 4.0 GHz)
specs.ports: 3x USB4 Type-C (DP 2.1, PD), HDMI 2.1b, headset jack

battery.notes: Estimated; RTX Spark platform battery criticised in press, no verified CA figure.

price.notes: VERIFIED dell.ca 2026-11-24: CAD $5,799.99 (est. value $6,599.99, $800 off). A 128GB/2TB tier exists at $8,899.99 (omitted).

reviews.quote: No professional review of this exact RTX Spark XPS 16 SKU as of 2026-11; ratings inferred from the CNET XPS 16 (2026) chassis anchor and RTX Spark platform coverage.

praises: 64GB unified memory + RTX 6144-core GPU is the best out-of-the-box local-LLM laptop in Dell's entire consumer range
Runs 70B-class quantized models locally that 32GB machines cannot load
SDXC + HDMI 2.1b + USB4 covers creator I/O natively
3.2K OLED 1000-nit touch panel doubles as a calibrated-grade reference display
$1,000 below the 128GB tier, which most buyers do not need
complaints: Arm Windows translation caveats remain for pro audio plugins and anti-cheat games despite the powerful GPU
$5,800 puts it against MacBook Pro 14 M-series Max with stronger battery
Press consensus on the RTX Spark platform is mixed on battery life
~2.1 kg / 17.8 mm — heavier than the standard XPS 16 OLED
Soldered memory: paying $1,000 for the 64GB you cannot later add

design_philosophy: The memory-max Creator Edition: Dell's flagship statement that a Windows creator laptop should unify CPU, RTX GPU, and large memory pool in one thin chassis for on-device AI. Aimed at developers and AI tinkerers who want CUDA locally without a workstation.
rating_notes: Inferred from sibling 32GB Creator Edition (entry 52) + CNET XPS 16 chassis anchor: 64GB unified memory → ai_ml +0.5 (9.5), productivity +0.5 (9.5). Arm ecosystem caveat 7.5 per NOTES calibration. Battery/weight estimated.
